correctness.rationale: For any zero-free rank-two generator, conditioning on the first sampled projective class gives exactly \(1+\sum_i m_i/(n-m_i)\). A zero column is strictly dominated by replacement with an existing nonzero direction because a subsequent independent direction gives a positive-probability strict improvement. The discrete increment of \(f(t)=t/(n-t)\) is strictly increasing, so every pair with gap at least two is strictly improved by transferring one column from the larger to the smaller multiplicity. Iteration proves both the balanced optimum and uniqueness of its multiplicity multiset. The packaged exact composition replay for small parameters was independently checked as finite consistency evidence, not as proof of the all-parameter theorem.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality passes. The comprehensive March 2026 primary paper defines the same all-code optimum, proves the MDS lower bound, and still states simplex optimality as a conjecture in the small-field regime. Its fixed-family formulas do not optimize arbitrary rank-two multisets once repeated projective directions are forced. The 2023 MDS theorem covers the rank-two parameters only through the MDS-feasible range. Fresh Resultary search found no prior balanced-projective-multiplicity optimizer theorem.
